zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly equates two attribute values (e.g., "Arnold loves baseball"), treat them as a single combined entity and assign both attributes to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue states that two attributes belong to the same person.
zebralogic.example: Treating "Bob paints" and "Bob's education is bachelor's" as unrelated constraints, missing that Bob's hobby and education must be placed together.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue pins an attribute to a specific house number, place that attribute at the indicated house right away and propagate any linked attributes.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a concrete house index (e.g., "the Honda Civic is in the third house").
zebralogic.example: Delaying placement of the Honda Civic despite the clue "the Honda Civic is in the third house", leading to later contradictions.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Clues using "next to", "directly left of", or "directly right of" require the referenced houses to be adjacent in the specified order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions adjacency or a direct left/right relationship.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "the person who enjoys knitting is directly left of the person with a high school diploma" as allowing a gap between the two houses.

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: The final answer must be a JSON object with a "header" array describing column order and a "rows" array of house entries, matching the verifier's expected format.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the end of reasoning, before returning the answer.
zebralogic.example: Providing the solution as plain text without the required "header" and "rows" fields, causing the verifier to reject it.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: Limit explanatory text before the final answer so the response stays within the model's token budget and does not truncate the output.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When the reasoning becomes lengthy; ensure the final JSON is included in full.
zebralogic.example: Generating a long chain of reasoning that exceeds the token limit, resulting in the final JSON being cut off or omitted.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the prompt, preserving capitalization, spacing, hyphens, and other characters.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, ensure attribute strings match the prompt verbatim.
zebralogic.example: Writing "Ford F150" instead of the exact token "ford f150", causing a mismatch with the verifier.

zebralogic.title: Interpret Directional Ordering Correctly
zebralogic.principle: Distinguish between "somewhere to the left of" (non‑adjacent ordering) and "directly left of" (adjacent ordering) and apply the correct constraint.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses directional language such as left/right or somewhere left/right.
zebralogic.example: Treating "somewhere to the left of" as requiring immediate adjacency, misplacing houses.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exclusion Constraints for Specific House Numbers
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a particular house, treat that as a hard exclusion and never place that attribute there.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says "X is not in house N" or similar.
zebralogic.example: Placing the soccer lover in house 1 despite the clue "the person who loves soccer is not in the first house".

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exact Distance Constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue specifies an exact number of houses between two attributes (e.g., "two houses between X and Y"), enforce that precise distance.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a numeric distance between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the clue "two houses between X and Y" and placing X directly next to Y.

zebralogic.title: Chain Direct Equivalences Across Multiple Clues
zebralogic.principle: When multiple direct equivalence clues share attributes, treat the whole set as a single equivalence group, allowing transitive inference that all linked attributes belong to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever you have two or more direct equivalence clues that can be linked through a common attribute.
zebralogic.example: Failing to infer that the craftsman house occupant's child is Meredith from the two clues "Craftsman ↔ average height" and "average height ↔ child Meredith".

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing token truncation.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to elaborate on deductions without reserving space for the required JSON output, exceeding the token budget.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Limit the length of explanatory text and place the final JSON answer as early as possible within the response.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses "somewhere to the left of" with "directly left of", treating non‑adjacent ordering as adjacency.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Explicitly distinguish between adjacency and non‑adjacent ordering; apply adjacency only when the clue says "directly".

zebralogic.description: Treating adjacency clues as non‑adjacent ordering, leading to placement errors.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model applies a generic ordering rule to clues that actually require immediate adjacency.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue uses "next to", "directly left of", or "directly right of", enforce that the houses are consecutive.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting exact distance clues (e.g., "one house between") as adjacency or ignoring the distance.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model overlooks the numeric distance requirement and treats the relationship as simple ordering.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue specifies a numeric gap, enforce that exact number of houses between the two referenced attributes.
